ground_truth.name: get_signature
ground_truth.note: SigningAlgorithm.get_signature (signer.py:20, the abstract base's own body, which unconditionally raises NotImplementedError) is a third reachable candidate: SigningAlgorithm is not decorated with @abstractmethod/ABC, so `Signer(secret, algorithm=SigningAlgorithm())` is valid Python with no enforcement preventing it, unlike e.g. chevrotain's structurally analogous GAstVisitor case where TypeScript's `abstract class` keyword blocks direct instantiation at compile time. Found during an independent reverification pass (2026-09-04) that the original ground_truth list omitted.

verification.verification_note: self.algorithm (signer.py:173) is typed SigningAlgorithm but is duck-typed in the Python sense: any instance assigned to it - default HMACAlgorithm (signer.py:171), or NoneAlgorithm, or a caller-supplied SigningAlgorithm subclass passed via the public `algorithm=` constructor parameter - determines which get_signature body actually runs at signer.py:219's self.algorithm.get_signature(key, value), and nothing at that call site distinguishes them. No single ground_truth candidate is correct in isolation; NoneAlgorithm.get_signature, HMACAlgorithm.get_signature, and (since SigningAlgorithm is not decorated with @abstractmethod/ABC and can be instantiated directly) the abstract base's own get_signature are all equally valid targets from source alone. This is the Python duck-typing counterpart to hyperfine-06 and corbel-05's Rust dyn-trait dispatch, and structurally identical to the already-adversarial hyperfine-12/hyperfine-38 dyn-trait cases. Originally logged as a legacy (pre-difficulty-field) entry without a difficulty tag; classified `adversarial` on 2026-09-03 once its structural match to those cases was recognized, coincidentally completing the golden set's adversarial quota at the same time - the technical basis for the classification is the duck-typed dispatch itself, independent of and unaffected by where the count happened to land.

ground_truth.name: __init__
ground_truth.note: Serializer.make_signer (serializer.py:278-285) constructs the active signer as `self.signer(self.secret_keys, salt=salt, **self.signer_kwargs)` at serializer.py:285, where `self.signer: type[Signer]` is a class attribute set from the `signer` constructor parameter (default `Signer`, serializer.py:99 `default_signer: type[Signer] = Signer`; overridable per-Serializer-instance). The call `self.signer(...)` is a constructor call on a type held in a variable, not a textual `Signer(` or `.__init__(` anywhere in the source - no name-based or AST call-site search targeting the literal identifier `__init__` or `Signer` will find serializer.py:285 as a call to this symbol. Within this repository specifically, the only two classes ever assigned to `self.signer` are `Signer` itself and `TimestampSigner` (timed.py:22), and TimestampSigner defines no `__init__` of its own, so in practice both possible runtime classes execute this exact Signer.__init__ - but that is an accident of this codebase's current class hierarchy, not something provable from the call site at serializer.py:285 alone (a third-party subclass with its own __init__ passed via the public `signer=` constructor argument would silently redirect it).

impact.note: Filled in during schema-validation pass (2026-09-03), missing from the original entry. serializer.py:285 (`self.signer(self.secret_keys, salt=salt, **self.signer_kwargs)`, inside Serializer.make_signer, serializer.py:278) is the one real call site reaching Signer.__init__ (or TimestampSigner.__init__) via the self.signer class-attribute indirection documented in this entry's ground_truth.

ground_truth.name: sign
ground_truth.note: self.make_signer(salt).sign(payload) at serializer.py:315, inside the base Serializer.dumps. make_signer's declared return type is `Signer` (serializer.py:278: `def make_signer(...) -> Signer`), so pyright's type-aware reference resolution statically attributes this call to Signer.sign (this entry). But make_signer's actual body returns `self.signer(...)` where `self.signer: type[Signer]` is a class attribute (see itsdangerous-11's Signer.__init__ entry for the same attribute). TimedSerializer overrides it: `default_signer: type[TimestampSigner] = TimestampSigner  # pyright: ignore` (timed.py:175) - note the `# pyright: ignore`, meaning pyright itself flags this override as a type error, because it narrows `type[Signer]` to the incompatible `type[TimestampSigner]`. TimestampSigner overrides `sign` (timed.py:45). So for any TimedSerializer or TimedJSONWebSignatureSerializer instance, the object returned by self.make_signer(salt) is actually a TimestampSigner at runtime, and `.sign(payload)` genuinely executes TimestampSigner.sign, not this entry's Signer.sign - a real static/dynamic mismatch, not merely an untyped duck-typing gap: pyright's own declared-type answer is provably wrong for a subset of the class hierarchy it already ships with an acknowledged type-checker suppression.
